prompt: What gives a country an absolute advantage in producing a good?

options.label: A
options.text: More output from the same resources.

options.label: B
options.text: Lower opportunity cost than foreign producers.

options.label: C
options.text: A larger export volume than imports.

options.label: D
options.text: Higher selling prices than foreign producers.

explanation: Absolute advantage compares physical productivity using the same resources. A country has an absolute advantage when those resources can produce a larger quantity of the good.

prompt: What gives a country a comparative advantage in producing a good?

options.label: A
options.text: Higher output per worker in all goods.

options.label: B
options.text: Lower opportunity cost than another country.

options.label: C
options.text: A larger labour force than trading partners.

options.label: D
options.text: Lower import prices than export prices.

explanation: Comparative advantage is determined by opportunity cost, not simply by the absolute quantity that can be produced.
reference: 6.1 The reasons for international trade | 6.1.1 distinction between absolute and comparative advantage | AO1 Knowledge and understanding

prompt: Country A can produce more wheat and more steel than country B with the same resources. Which statement must be correct?

options.label: A
options.text: Country A has an absolute advantage in both goods.

options.label: B
options.text: Country A has a comparative advantage in both goods.

options.label: C
options.text: Country B cannot gain from trade with country A.

options.label: D
options.text: Country B has an absolute advantage in at least one good.

explanation: Producing more of each good with the same resources gives A an absolute advantage in both. Comparative advantage still depends on relative opportunity costs, so it need not belong to A in both goods.
reference: 6.1 The reasons for international trade | 6.1.1 distinction between absolute and comparative advantage | AO1 Knowledge and understanding

prompt: Which statement about comparative advantage is correct?

options.label: A
options.text: Absolute advantage is necessary for comparative advantage.

options.label: B
options.text: Comparative advantage does not require absolute advantage.

options.label: C
options.text: Exporting a good proves comparative advantage in it.

options.label: D
options.text: Money wages alone determine comparative advantage.

explanation: Comparative advantage is based on relative opportunity cost. A less productive country can still be relatively less inefficient in one activity and therefore have a comparative advantage in it.
reference: 6.1 The reasons for international trade | 6.1.1 distinction between absolute and comparative advantage | AO1 Knowledge and understanding
